{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire sub_ab = (Oper == 3'b001);
    wire sub_ba = (Oper == 3'b010);
    wire subtract = sub_ab | sub_ba;
    wire [63:0] x = a ^ {64{sub_ba}};
    wire [63:0] y = b ^ {64{sub_ab}};
    wire [63:0] p = x ^ y;
    wire [63:0] g = x & y;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result;

    // Four-bit group propagate/generate, followed by a balanced
    // prefix network across the sixteen groups.
    wire [15:0] group_p [0:4];
    wire [15:0] group_g [0:4];
    wire [15:0] group_cin;

    genvar k, s, n;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : groups
            wire [3:0] pp = p[4*k +: 4];
            wire [3:0] gg = g[4*k +: 4];
            wire [3:0] c;

            assign group_p[0][k] = &pp;
            assign group_g[0][k] = gg[3]
                | (pp[3] & gg[2])
                | (pp[3] & pp[2] & gg[1])
                | (pp[3] & pp[2] & pp[1] & gg[0]);

            assign c[0] = group_cin[k];
            assign c[1] = gg[0] | (pp[0] & c[0]);
            assign c[2] = gg[1] | (pp[1] & gg[0])
                | (pp[1] & pp[0] & c[0]);
            assign c[3] = gg[2] | (pp[2] & gg[1])
                | (pp[2] & pp[1] & gg[0])
                | (pp[2] & pp[1] & pp[0] & c[0]);
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k +: 4] = pp ^ c;
        end

        for (s = 0; s < 4; s = s + 1) begin : prefix_levels
            for (n = 0; n < 16; n = n + 1) begin : prefix_nodes
                if (n >= (1 << s)) begin : combine
                    assign group_g[s+1][n] = group_g[s][n]
                        | (group_p[s][n] & group_g[s][n-(1 << s)]);
                    assign group_p[s+1][n] = group_p[s][n]
                        & group_p[s][n-(1 << s)];
                end else begin : passthrough
                    assign group_g[s+1][n] = group_g[s][n];
                    assign group_p[s+1][n] = group_p[s][n];
                end
            end
        end

        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : group_carries
            if (k == 0) begin : first
                assign group_cin[k] = subtract;
            end else begin : remaining
                assign group_cin[k] = group_g[4][k-1]
                    | (group_p[4][k-1] & subtract);
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        case (Oper)
            3'b000, 3'b001, 3'b010: sum = arithmetic_result;
            3'b011: sum = a | b;
            3'b100: sum = a & b;
            3'b101: sum = a ^ b;
            3'b110: sum = a ~^ b;
            default: sum = 64'b0;
        endcase
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": {
    "hypothesis": "The arithmetic carry-generation network and its final result-selection logic are the likely timing bottleneck.",
    "supporting_evidence": "The measured worst paths run from a[5] to widely separated upper result bits sum[47], sum[54], and sum[55], reaching 3.04–3.05 ns through long shared NAND/NOR/AOI/OAI networks. The sum[54] path includes a late XOR followed by selection-like complex gates. The conservative pre-ABC cone contains arithmetic operators and a result pmux, consistent with this hypothesis.",
    "precision_limit": "The evidence does not identify exact mapped carry or mux cells and does not establish serial adders. The three source arithmetic operators can be restructured by Yosys and ABC."
  },
  "rewrite": "Use one configurable modulo-2^64 arithmetic datapath. Addition uses a+b; a-b uses a+~b+1; b-a uses ~a+b+1. Carry generation is explicitly organized as four-bit local lookahead, four prefix levels across sixteen groups, and local carry expansion. This avoids an operand-swapping mux and expresses bounded-depth carry dependencies while retaining the original logical operations and output selection. ABC remains free to restructure and map this network.",
  "expected_timing_gain": {
    "hypothesis": "A plausible exploratory target is approximately 0.2–0.6 ns less maximum data arrival than the 3.05 ns baseline, but this is not a measured result or a guaranteed range.",
    "reason": "The explicit grouped prefix structure may reduce long arithmetic dependencies, while sharing arithmetic may reduce duplicated logic and loading. Operand-conditioning XORs, select fanout, prefix loading, and final output selection can offset those benefits.",
    "required_validation": "Run full equivalence, then the exact supplied synthesis, mapping, and OpenSTA flow. Compare maximum data arrival across all input-to-output paths, including Oper paths; do not use the positive virtual-clock slack as the optimization metric."
  },
  "area_or_other_cost": {
    "area_cap_um2": 13098.43744,
    "baseline_area_um2": 11907.6704,
    "available_area_increase_um2": 1190.76704,
    "tradeoff": "Sharing arithmetic creates a plausible area budget for prefix logic, but prefix nodes, operand-conditioning gates, and buffering have costs. No mapped area estimate or cap compliance is established without EDA.",
    "eligibility": "This is an unvalidated candidate, not a demonstrated passing implementation. Accept it only after full functional equivalence, mapped area at or below the cap, zero max-slew violations, zero max-capacitance violations, and improved maximum data arrival under the fixed flow."
  },
  "functional_boundaries": {
    "interface": "Preserves module alu_64bit, 64-bit inputs a and b, 3-bit input Oper, and 64-bit output reg sum.",
    "operations": {
      "000": "a+b modulo 2^64",
      "001": "a-b modulo 2^64",
      "010": "b-a modulo 2^64",
      "011": "a OR b",
      "100": "a AND b",
      "101": "a XOR b",
      "110": "a XNOR b",
      "111": "zero"
    },
    "constraints": "Purely combinational, with no clocks, state, input restrictions, assumptions, or don't-cares. The original internal c_out is omitted because it is not observable at any output. No carry-out or overflow behavior is added to the interface."
  }
}
